For at least the last three or four months, pretty much every week—usually a couple of times a week—I’ll have these episodes at night after my husband goes to bed. I’ll go through half a loaf of bread, cereal, cookies, whatever’s in the kitchen, in maybe 30–40 minutes. I’m not even hungry; it feels like I can’t stop until I’m uncomfortably full and almost in pain.

Right after, I panic about the calories and what it’s going to do to my thighs, my stomach, my face. When I look in the mirror, I see someone much bigger than what other people tell me they see. I feel disgusting, huge. Then I go to the bathroom and make myself throw up. I’ve been doing that at least once a week, often more, during these months.

Alongside this, my mood’s been really low—dragging myself to work, feeling guilty and hopeless, crying in the car, trouble enjoying anything. But what I obsess about the most is my weight and shape and undoing the damage from those binges.

I’m exhausted all the time, but my sleep is broken—up at 3 a.m., mind racing with guilt about being “useless” or a burden.

My appetite’s changed in a weird way. Some evenings I’ll suddenly eat way more than I normally would—a whole pizza plus leftovers, finishing my kids’ food—almost mechanically, like I’m trying to fill some hole. But I don’t make myself throw up or use laxatives or anything like that, and I’m not obsessing over my weight or shape when I do it. I just feel disgusting and ashamed afterward and even more down on myself.

At work I make careless mistakes, which scares me in my job. Concentrating on simple labels or calculations takes so much effort. Some mornings I honestly wonder if everyone would be better off without me.
